title: Changes in Snow Resources of Western Kazakhstan in the Context of Global Warming
content: Global climate change impacts snow and ice resources and the frequency and timing of dangerous hydrological phenomena. The article presents the results of a study of snow resource variability in Western Kazakhstan in the context of global warming. The research aims to assess the impact of global climate change on regional snow cover conditions. Statistical analysis methods were used to assess these effects. A database of snow and regional climate was collected. The statistical error of the initial data was 2-4%. It was established that snowmelt runoff from rivers mainly forms in the low-mountain areas of Mugalzhary in the north of the Aktobe region and on the Podural plateau in the north of the West Kazakhstan region. This affects the timing of the spring flood. However, these trends are not statistically significant (the coefficient of determination is 0.02-0.24) and their value is within the statistical errors. The calculated Spearman statistics prove the existence of a statistical relationship between global and regional climate indicators (correlation coefficients 0.23-0.40). Changes, but it is influenced by many local factors. This must be taken into account when planning economic activities in the region.
